req.title: Status code sentence body
req.statement: The system shall include the standard reason phrase in the body when responding to /status/<code> with a code between 400 and 599.

doc.reasoning: R-HTTPBIN-045 requires that GET /status/<code> for codes 400-599 returns a response whose body contains the standard HTTP reason phrase. The status_code() helper in helpers.py builds the response; for most codes it leaves r.data empty (no explicit data set), but the requirement says the reason phrase must appear. We must test: (1) a typical 4xx code (positive EP), (2) a typical 5xx code (positive EP), (3) the exact boundary codes 400 and 599 (BVA ±1: 399 is outside range, 400 is first in range, 599 is last, 600 is outside), (4) a code just outside the range (NEG), and (5) special codes with overridden data (DT: 402, 406, 418) to ensure their bodies still satisfy the requirement. We also assert the HTTP response status code equals the requested code exactly, catching off-by-one and comparison-flip mutations. The reason phrases are taken from the standard HTTP spec (RFC 7231 / IANA registry).

tests.name: test_status_400_body_contains_reason_phrase
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /status/400 is a valid endpoint
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 400
Response body contains 'BAD REQUEST' (case-insensitive)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-045: 400 is in [400,599]; body must contain standard reason phrase 'Bad Request'
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_400_body_contains_reason_phrase():
    r = client.get('/status/400')
    assert r.status_code == 400
    body = r.data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    assert 'BAD REQUEST' in body.upper() or 'Bad Request' in body
